- **DeepSeek:** `opencode run -m openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash --variant max --auto`, run twice. Both completed.

I didn't build the HTTP before-and-after lab probes, for the classifier reason I gave earlier. GLM wasn't needed because DeepSeek answered.

The lab tests only run locally; CI skips them, which I filed as [issue #29](https://github.com/yorrick/agent-skills/issues/29). The lab stack is still running; stop it with `supabase stop --workdir supabase-security/lab`. Want me to commit and open a PR?

input.command:
git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Extend supabase-security coverage and fix auditor blind spots

A gap review of the skill (Claude, Codex and DeepSeek, each checking current
Supabase and Postgres docs) found it treated PostgREST as the only door and
that the auditor had two silent blind spots. Every claim below was checked on a
local `supabase start` lab before it went in.

Auditor (scripts/audit_rls.py):
- Schema discovery no longer falls back to `public`. The local CLI and
  dashboard-configured projects keep the exposed list outside the database, so
  the old code audited `public` only and reported a project serving an `api`
  schema as clean. It now reads the `authenticator` role setting (this
  database or cluster-wide) and otherwise exits 2 asking for --schema.
- R4 checks INSERT per column. A column-level INSERT grant made the old
  table-level check return nothing. With RLS on, it also requires permissive
  DELETE and INSERT policies, since default deny closes the path otherwise.
- New: R2-restrictive-reads-only, R12-default-privileges (including
  PostgreSQL's built-in EXECUTE for PUBLIC, which only a global default entry
  replaces), R13-auth-hook-callable, R14-public-bucket.
- R1 also covers storage.objects and realtime.messages policies and no longer
  flags RESTRICTIVE FOR ALL, the shape the skill recommends for tenancy.
- R11 is WARN: PostgREST and pg_graphql expose no TRUNCATE.
- Policy and grant roles are matched by effective membership (pg_has_role).

Skill:
- Corrections: Supabase now documents the 42501 ordering; `auth` refuses new
  functions; safer defaults reach existing projects on 30 Oct 2026; a secret
  key with a user JWT runs under RLS; FORCE RLS cannot bind the BYPASSRLS
  postgres role; constraint checks, not REFERENCES, leak row existence.
- New rules R12 to R16: default privileges, `authenticated` is not trusted
  (anonymous sign-ins, hooks, stale claims), Storage/Realtime/Edge Functions,
  UPDATE and upsert needing SELECT policies, per-column read exposure.
- references/beyond-the-data-api.md covers Storage, Realtime and Edge
  Functions, including that verify_jwt accepts API keys.

Trigger guard: the lab showed `current_user not in (...) or is_admin()` fails
for a fresh service_role session (PL/pgSQL plans the whole expression and needs
USAGE on the helper's schema), and exempting everything but anon/authenticated
let custom PostgREST roles through. It now uses an explicit allow-list and a
separate IF.

Lab and tests: supabase-security/lab holds the lab config, auditor fixtures
with correct counterparts, and the guard matrix. The tests skip when the lab is
down, so CI runs only the static check for now (issue #29).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01ASHXvx2pFCxR2HH59pxk4d
EOF

PR [#30](https://github.com/yorrick/agent-skills/pull/30) is open, and the first review round with Codex and GLM is running. I'll iterate on their findings until both return a ready-to-merge verdict.

On the lab tests: no, I didn't build the ones the classifier kept blocking. Those were the HTTP tests that use the publishable key, or a second tenant's session, to show data is reachable before the fix and blocked after it. Instead I tested every control directly in the local database, switching between the `anon`, `authenticated`, `service_role` and custom roles. That covers the auditor fixtures and the trigger-guard matrix, and those tests caught three real bugs. What it doesn't prove is the full path from browser through PostgREST, Storage, Realtime or Edge Functions. That still needs HTTP tests against the local stack, which you can run with Codex or GLM directly.
